slides.title: Clear Visuals for Complex Evidence
bullets: Visual communication of evidence is a constant Medical Affairs need
Ranges from a pivotal study infographic to a congress data presentation
AI design tools have lowered the technical barrier to producing them
Reduces dependence on a dedicated graphic design team

slides.title: From Description to Draft Visual
bullets: Generate infographic drafts, mechanism-of-action visuals, or slide templates
Works from a natural language description or a reference document
Drafts are then refined and verified by the MSL or scientific comms team
Frees time for refinement and verification instead of creation from scratch

slides.title: Support Material for Your Own Use
bullets: Visual schemes to explain a complex mechanism of action in conversation
Visual summaries of key study data to carry into a visit
Support material for an internal congress debrief presentation
Only within what internal policy allows without formal MLR review

slides.title: External or Formal Material Needs MLR Review
bullets: Anything distributed externally to an HCP requires full MLR review
Same standard applies as any other scientific material in Module 10
Ease of AI generation does not exempt it from compliance control
Skipping review exposes the MSL and the organization to real risk

slides.title: AI Generates the Form, Not the Facts
bullets: Any data or scientific claim in a visual still needs full verification
Visual generation tools do not check the accuracy of the content
Responsibility for data accuracy remains entirely human and professional

takeaway.title: Canva AI speeds up visual drafts, but MLR review and data accuracy stay non-negotiable
bullets: Best for personal field-use visuals within internal policy limits
Any externally distributed or formal material still needs full MLR review
The MSL, not the tool, is responsible for every number and claim shown
